from.place: The higher derived functors of an exact functor followed by a left-exact functor are the derived functors of the latter evaluated after the exact functor.

title: Derived functors after an exact functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories, and suppose $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ have enough injectives. Let $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be exact and suppose that $T(I)$ is $U$-acyclic for every injective $I$ of $\mathcal A$, where $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is left exact. Using the right-derived-functor convention of [def-sp-left-exact-additive], for every object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ and every $i\geq0$, the $i$-th right derived functor of $U\circ T$ at $M$ is canonically isomorphic to the $i$-th right derived functor of $U$ evaluated at $T(M)$. The notions of abelian category, injective resolution, and acyclicity are those of [def-sp-abelian], [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and [def-sp-acyclic].

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Since $T$ is exact, applying it to the augmented exact sequence gives an exact sequence $0\to T(M)\to T(I^0)\to T(I^1)\to\cdots$. Thus $T(I^\bullet)$ is a resolution of $T(M)$, bounded below and with the same degrees as $I^\bullet$; its terms need not be injective in $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Lemma 015M (derived-lemma-compose-derived-functors), proof: choose an injective resolution and apply the first functor

proof.text: By the hypothesis on $T$, every term $T(I^m)$ of the resolution in Step 1 is $U$-acyclic in the sense of [def-sp-acyclic]. Apply item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] with $v=U$, $F=T(M)$ and the resolution $T(M)\to T(I^\bullet)$. Its natural comparison gives $R^iU(T(M))\cong\mathcal H^i(U(T(I^\bullet)))$ for every $i\geq0$; it does not require $T(I^m)$ to be injective.

source.place: Lemma 015M (derived-lemma-compose-derived-functors), proof, final appeal to Lemma 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity)

proof.text: The composite $U\circ T$ is left exact: $T$ preserves kernels and finite biproducts because it is exact, and $U$ preserves them by left exactness [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Computing its right derived functor with the chosen injective resolution gives $R^i(U\circ T)(M)=\mathcal H^i(U(T(I^\bullet)))$. The comparison of Step 2 therefore gives the claimed isomorphism. The isomorphism is the natural map of item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], induced by any morphism of complexes $T(I^\bullet)\to J^\bullet$ over $\mathrm{id}_{T(M)}$ into an injective resolution $T(M)\to J^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; it is in this sense canonical, the derived functors on both sides being those of the convention of [def-sp-left-exact-additive].
